# astralis-cli

Setup and tooling CLI for [Astralis UI](https://astralis-zeta.vercel.app): start
a project, wire the library into an existing one, copy in blocks, generate a
static theme, check code against the design system, and connect AI agents.

```bash
npx astralis-cli <command>
# or: npm i -g astralis-cli && astralis <command>
```

Needs Node `^22.18` or `>=24.11`. Run `astralis <command> --help` for any
command's options. Full guide: <https://astralis-zeta.vercel.app/docs/cli>.

## Commands

<!-- reference:start (generated by scripts/reference.mjs; edit src/lib/commands.mjs) -->

### `astralis create <name>`

Scaffold a new project with create-next-app or create-vite and wire Astralis into it.

| Option | |
| --- | --- |
| `--framework <next\|vite>` | Skip the framework prompt. |
| `--no-starter` | Keep the scaffolder's demo page instead of the Astralis welcome screen. |
| `--no-devtools` | Leave out the Astralis DevTools overlay, which new projects get in development. |

Any other argument passes straight to the scaffolder.

```bash
astralis create my-app
astralis create my-app --framework vite --template react
```

### `astralis init`

Wire astralis-ui into an existing Next.js or React + Vite project.

| Option | |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | Show the changes without writing anything. |
| `--ci` | Also check every pull request: pin astralis-cli, add a validate script and write a GitHub Actions workflow. |
| `--force` | With --ci, replace an existing astralis-validate.yml. |
| `--devtools` | Also add the Astralis DevTools overlay (development only): install astralis-devtools and wire it into the root layout or vite.config. |

init --ci is safe to re-run: it adds only what is missing and never replaces a workflow without --force.

init --devtools is safe to re-run too; production builds contain none of the DevTools.

```bash
astralis init
astralis init --dry-run
astralis init --ci
astralis init --devtools
```

### `astralis add <block...>`

Copy a block's source into this project.

| Option | |
| --- | --- |
| `--list` | Print every available block, by category, and exit. |
| `--dir <path>` | Where to write. Default: src/components/blocks, or components/blocks without a src/. |
| `--overwrite` | Replace existing files without asking. |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be written; write nothing. |
| `--registry <url>` | Read blocks from a different registry host. |

```bash
astralis add hero-01
astralis add login-01 dashboard-02 --dir src/ui/blocks
astralis add --list
```

### `astralis theme [hex]`

Generate a static theme stylesheet from a seed.

| Option | |
| --- | --- |
| `--brand <hex>` | Brand hue, e.g. "#8b5cf6". A bare hex argument means the same. |
| `--gray <hex>` | Neutral hue: every surface, label and border. |
| `--error <hex>` | Seeds the error palette. Default: red. |
| `--warning <hex>` | Seeds the warning palette. Default: orange. |
| `--success <hex>` | Seeds the success palette. Default: green. |
| `--info <hex>` | Seeds the info palette. Default: blue. |
| `--font-heading <stack>` | Heading font stack. |
| `--font-body <stack>` | Body font stack. |
| `--font-mono <stack>` | Monospace font stack. |
| `--radius <n>` | Border-radius multiplier. Default: 1. |
| `--spacing <n>` | Spacing multiplier: the density dial. Default: 1. |
| `--font-scale <n>` | Font-size multiplier. Default: 1. |
| `--motion <n>` | Duration multiplier; 0 turns transitions off. Default: 1. |
| `--out <file>` | Where to write the stylesheet. Default: src/astralis-theme.css, or astralis-theme.css without a src/. |
| `--force` | Overwrite an existing file. |
| `--no-import` | Write the file but leave the entry file alone. |
| `--strict-contrast` | Exit 1, writing nothing, if any promised pairing fails WCAG AA. |

The status hues' own colorScheme values are never altered; each status seeds its own palette.

```bash
astralis theme "#8b5cf6"
astralis theme --brand "#8b5cf6" --gray "#64748b" --radius 1.5
```

### `astralis validate [paths...]`

Check TSX and JSX against the installed design system.

| Option | |
| --- | --- |
| `--format <text\|json\|github>` | How to report: text for people, json for tools, github for inline pull-request annotations. Default: github inside GitHub Actions, text elsewhere. |
| `--json` | Same as --format json. |
| `--spec <path>` | Validate against this system-spec.json. Default: the installed astralis-ui's. |
| `--strict-tokens` | Also warn on raw colors that bypass the tokens. |

With no paths it checks the current directory, skipping node_modules and build output.

Exits 1 when there are errors; warnings are reported but never fail the run.

```bash
astralis validate
astralis validate src/components --json
astralis validate --strict-tokens
```

### `astralis report <files...>`

Report a problem to the Astralis maintainers, with a snapshot built from your source files.

| Option | |
| --- | --- |
| `--title <text>` | The report's title. Asked for when omitted; required with --yes. |
| `--happened <text>` | What happened. |
| `--expected <text>` | What you expected instead. |
| `--include-text` | Keep the text in your JSX; by default it is replaced by placeholders. |
| `--no-findings` | Leave out the validator's findings for these files. |
| `--out <file>` | Write the snapshot to a file instead of sending it. |
| `--dry-run` | Print the snapshot and send nothing. |
| `--spec <path>` | Build against this system-spec.json. Default: the installed astralis-ui's. |

It prints the exact JSON first and sends nothing until you confirm; --yes confirms without asking.

Only literal props are recorded, and only those the spec describes; links, sources and handlers never are.

```bash
astralis report app/page.tsx
astralis report src/App.tsx --title "Card loses its border" --out snapshot.json
```

### `astralis connect-mcp`

Connect an AI coding agent to the Astralis MCP docs server.

| Option | |
| --- | --- |
| `--client <claude-code\|codex\|cursor\|claude-desktop\|antigravity>` | Skip the prompt and configure this client. |

```bash
astralis connect-mcp
astralis connect-mcp --client cursor --yes
```

### Global options

Every command takes these.

| Option | |
| --- | --- |
| `-y, --yes` | Never prompt; take the default answer. Replacing files still needs --overwrite or --force. |
| `-h, --help` | Show this command's options. |
| `--debug` | Print the stack trace if something fails unexpectedly. |

<!-- reference:end -->

## `validate` in CI

`astralis validate` exits `1` when it finds an error and `0` otherwise;
warnings never fail the run. `--json` prints one report:

```json
{
  "spec": { "name": "astralis-ui", "version": "0.7.8", "specVersion": 1 },
  "files": 12,
  "errors": 1,
  "warnings": 0,
  "results": [
    {
      "file": "src/app/page.tsx",
      "errors": [
        { "code": "invalid-recipe-value", "file": "src/app/page.tsx", "line": 8, "column": 15,
          "message": "Button: \"primary\" is not a variant value (valid: link, text, subtle, solid, surface, outline)" }
      ],
      "warnings": []
    }
  ]
}
```

`results` lists only files with findings. The same checks are importable:
`astralis-cli/validate` (Node, with spec lookup) and `astralis-cli/validate-core`
(pure, browser-safe), both typed.
